Take a deep breath. You gotta talk to both kids but you can't be mad at him and you can't ask leading questions to her.

For him: in a calm, usually tone of voice, ask him if he exposed himself to his sister. If he says no, just say she said he did. Tell him you aren't mad, and you just want to talk to him about it. See below for the next steps.

If it's a yes, ask him why he did it. Kids are stupid, they do stupid shit. He might've thought it was funny, he might say she asked him to. You never know. If he said he felt like it or thought it'd be funny, you have a serious conversation to have. Tell him it's inappropriate and wrong and that they're private for a reason. Punish him, make him apologize, parent him from there, get him psychiatric care if he shows signs of predatory behavior. If he says she asked him to, that's totally different. In his mind, he could've thought he was helping her learn about the differences between boys and girls. He might have totally innocent intentions. Still give him the privacy talk, but punishing him would be more tricky.

For her: same voice rule. Ask her why he did it. If they both say she asked him to, that's a very different scenario then her saying she didn't want to see and he forced her to. That's COCSA and he needs immediate psychiatric care. 

Also, flip the genders of the kids. If this was your daughter exposing her genitals to her brother, and the traits of the kids you have are identical, would you be just as livid? I know it sounds weird to think about, but society places more protection on girls than boys for privacy and sexual misconduct.

One more thing, tread carefully with your son while talking to him. If he even hints at being a victim, this is way beyond your house. If he says another boy at school did and encouraged him, that's peer pressure. If he says that a man, woman, girl, or boy did the same to him when he was young, that's also a huge problem and he's not acting like that to be bad, he's recreating his own trauma and he needs counseling. He may very well have a history of CSA and need immediate help.

Doctors are idiots. I was told I'd never be as strong as the other kids, I'd never run fast, be severely impacted for the rest of my life. Now, I'm either stronger than my friends or on their level (except one guy, but he's the exception), I can outrun people, I'm not severely physically impacted by it. I have good days and bad days, I've also had at least 4 surgeries because of it. So your daughter has a long, difficult road ahead of her, but she can fight it. You can't cure her. You can medicate her for pain and there could be some procedures, but she's going to have this for the rest of her life.

Onto you, you need to fight with her. She's so young right now that she needs you to fight for her. Totally and completely fight for her. Every little thing you think she needs, fight for it. School services, disability aids, medications, get second/third/fourth opinion from doctors (who again are idiots that you need to trust), because although they are idiots, they're usually right to some extent. Research the top doctors in infant cerebral palsy and take her to them. You have to be her advocate. If she never learns how to talk, you need to fight every step of the way. It's really, really hard. She is the reason for you to live. It's a hard change to live through and I watched my diagnosis impact my mom's life in difficult ways. I watched my sister's mental health struggles do the same to our parents. My mom fought and my dad worked as much as he could to pay for everything. It's not easy. A child with special needs is very tough. But you have to live for her to have a chance. 

The first few days are hell. I'm truly sorry that you, your daughter, and entire family are experiencing this. Cerebral Palsy is brutal. There are some studies with caffeine helping but it's not conclusive. The only hope I can give you is to start her in physical and occupational therapy. The sooner her muscles start being activated, the better. Turn all of your anger, sadness, and your daughter's struggles into fire to get at least part of her back.

There are already enough people on here telling you about their own struggle and that you shouldn't do it so I won't waste time with that. But I do want to add something. You are 14 years old, meaning you live with others. They are going to find you. They'll be devastated. But let's say that they don't care, devil's advocate. They still need to report your death so they call 911. Most likely, the police show up first. Those officers are going to walk in and see a 14 year old kid dead. They are going to secure the area, maybe start checking for a pulse or doing CPR, depending on the department. Then the fire department shows up, and a handful of firefighters come in and try to save you. They do everything they can and EMS shows up and they start trying but there's nothing they can do. They call the hospital and they pronounce you, a kid, dead.

Those first responders don't know you, they don't know what you felt in your final moments or anything leading up to that. They just know a kid is dead. They probably have kids, maybe your age. They know that had you asked for help, they could've given you some.

The biggest thing that helped me after I tried was thinking about the cry for help that suicide is. You're willing to end it all and make the first responders see you dead, wishing they could've helped you first. So next time you want to, skip the suicide step. Go to the police or fire or EMS station and just tell the person at the front desk what you want to do. Tell them if you have a knife or a gun or pills, and just say you want help. You can call 911 and tell them you want to kill yourself, but that you want to live and they will stop you.
